cards.text: Ezekiel the prophet is in the middle of a vision of a new temple. Last time, he watched the glory of the God of Israel come into the temple through the gate facing east (Ezekiel 43:4). Now the man guiding him brings him back to that outer east gate, and it's shut.

cards.question: The LORD tells Ezekiel this east gate is to stay shut, and no man shall enter through it. Why?

answers.text: The LORD God of Israel has entered through it
Its doors were never finished being built
Enemies once broke into the city through it

cards.text: Nobody walks through that gate, and me, I wouldn't even LOOK at it too long. But the LORD makes one exception, and it isn't for walking through.

cards.question: Who may sit inside the shut east gateway to eat in the presence of the LORD?

cards.text: Even the prince comes in by way of the gateway's portico and goes out the same way. Then the man brings Ezekiel by the north gate to the front of the temple, and Ezekiel sees the glory of the LORD filling His temple.

cards.question: When Ezekiel sees the glory of the LORD filling His temple, he falls ___.

cards.text: Then the LORD tells him, 'Son of man, pay attention; look carefully with your eyes and listen closely with your ears…' Eyes AND ears, friend, that's put-the-phone-DOWN listening.

cards.question: The LORD tells Ezekiel to look carefully and listen closely. What is he supposed to take in?

answers.text: All the laws of the house of the LORD
The names of every priest in Israel
The songs sung in the temple courts

cards.text: Then comes a message for 'the rebellious house of Israel.' The Lord GOD says, 'I have had enough of all your abominations, O house of Israel.'

cards.question: On top of all their other abominations, who did the house of Israel bring in to occupy God's sanctuary?

answers.text: Foreigners uncircumcised in heart and flesh
Soldiers sent by the king of Babylon

cards.text: They defiled His temple while offering Him His food, the fat and the blood, and they broke His covenant.

cards.question: In His message, God says the house of Israel kept charge of His holy things themselves.
Under the Lord GOD's rule, even a foreigner who lives among the Israelites may not enter His sanctuary if he is uncircumcised in heart and flesh.

cards.text: Next, God speaks about the Levites, the tribe set apart to serve at His house (Numbers 3:6-9). The Levites who wandered away from Him after their idols will bear the consequences of their iniquity.

cards.question: Because they wandered after idols, these Levites will never minister in God's sanctuary at all.

cards.text: They'll have charge of the temple gates and slaughter the sacrifices for the people. But because they ministered before idols and became a stumbling block to Israel, God swore with an uplifted hand that they'd bear the consequences.

cards.question: The Levites who ministered before idols must not approach God to serve Him as ___.

cards.text: They can't come near His holy things, yet God still puts them in charge of all the work for the temple. That's losing the corner office but keeping the job, and from the back of my junk drawer I'd have taken that deal in a HEARTBEAT.
But one family of Levitical priests is different: the ones descended from Zadok. Zadok was a priest back in King David's day (2 Samuel 8:17).

cards.question: When the Israelites went astray from God, what did the priests descended from Zadok do?

answers.text: They kept charge of His sanctuary
They fled the land for Egypt

cards.text: Israel wandered off, and these priests just kept showing UP, which, friend, is half of any job. Now they'll stand before God to offer Him fat and blood.

cards.question: Only the priests descended from Zadok may enter God's sanctuary and draw near to His table.

cards.text: Then God gives the priests rules for how they live: linen and never wool, carefully trimmed hair, no wine before the inner court, and who they may marry. Before they go out to the people, they leave their holy garments in the holy chambers, so they don't pass holiness on to the people with their clothes.

cards.question: Besides serving before God, the priests are to teach His people the difference between the holy and the ___.
When God's people have a dispute, the priests are to judge it according to God's ordinances.

cards.text: They keep His laws for His appointed feasts and keep His Sabbaths holy. A priest stays away from the dead except for close family, and afterward he's cleansed, counts off seven days and presents a sin offering when he goes back in to minister.

cards.question: God speaks about what the priests will inherit. What does He say their inheritance is?
Along with that, Israel is to give the priests a possession in Israel.

cards.text: No possession in Israel, because God says, 'I am their possession.' I owned nothing but dust in that junk drawer, friend, and these priests own no land in Israel and have EVERYTHING.

They eat the grain offerings, sin offerings and guilt offerings, and the best of the firstfruits goes to them. Then God tells the people to give the priest their first batch of DOUGH, and friend, I have never felt so SEEN by a verse.

cards.question: Why are the people to give the priest their first batch of dough?

answers.text: So a blessing may rest on their homes
So the priests can feed the poor
So the next harvest comes in early

cards.text: One last rule: the priests may not eat any bird or animal found dead or torn by wild beasts. And that's where we'll leave the temple for now, friend, because Ezekiel's vision isn't done yet.

findings.problem: Card 1 says the glory of the God of Israel came into the temple through this east gate. Card 2 then asks why the east gate stays shut, and its right answer is 'The LORD God of Israel has entered through it.' The setup states the answer outright instead of giving context to reason from. Card 1 could set the scene, such as Ezekiel being led around the new temple, without saying what came through the gate.

rule.text: No card ever gives away the answer to a choice card that comes later.

findings.problem: The prince first appears in 44:3, and he is never introduced. Card 4 asks about 'The prince,' and card 5 says 'Even the prince…', but no card says simply who he is.

rule.text: New people. The first time someone shows up, he says simply who they are, like "Cyrus, king of Persia" or "Moses, Israel's leader."

findings.problem: 'linen and never wool' stretches the text. Ezekiel 44:17 forbids wool only 'when they minister at the gates of the inner court or inside the temple.' Verse 19 has the priests change into other clothes when they go out to the people.

rule.text: Don't stretch the text. Exaggerate only in his own jokes.

findings.problem: The blank asks the baker to finish the wording 'the difference between the holy and the ___' (44:23). This guesses the next word of a line rather than testing meaning. 'Foreign' is also easy to reason toward after the earlier ban on foreigners in 44:9.

rule.text: The rule against guessing the next words of a line (see below) applies to every passage, and to fill in the blank too. The blank tests meaning the baker can reason out, not wording they haven't seen.

findings.problem: The question opens with 'Along with that,' which points back to card 9, and card 9 is no longer on screen. The question should say what it builds on, such as God being the priests' inheritance.

rule.text: Always give context in the question. The story card before it isn't on screen anymore, so the question says who and what. Never "him," "that" or "it" pointing back to a card the baker can't see.
